items.text: Strict generators, continued: (b$'$) $\Rightarrow$ (b)
Assumption (b$'$): for every $X$, the family of all $Y\to X$, $Y\in C/X$, is strictly epimorphic.
F(X)\longrightarrow\prod_{Y\in C/X}F(Y)\quad\text{injective}
Strictly epimorphic says more: the image is cut out by a condition.
\begin{CD} T @>>> Y'\\ @VVV @VVV\\ Y'' @>>> X \end{CD}
For every square with $T\in E$ and $Y',Y''\in C/X$: $\;\xi_{Y'}|_T=\xi_{Y''}|_T$ in $F(T)$.
This is the condition for $F$ to be a sheaf for a topology.
To prove: $X=\varinjlim_{Y\in C/X}Y$, i.e. systems $(\xi_Y)$ compatible for $T\in C$ only are compatible for every $T$.
Take $T\notin C$: choose $(Y_i\to T)$, $Y_i\in C$, epimorphic; the two images agree in each $F(Y_i)$.
F(T)\hookrightarrow\prod_i F(Y_i)\ \Longrightarrow\ \xi_{Y'}|_T=\xi_{Y''}|_T
The SGA argument was right; the slip: an epimorphic family enlarged is not again strictly epimorphic.
Convenient for functorial arguments: (b$'$). Closer to ordinary terms: (c$'$), a strictly and universally epimorphic family with sources in $C$.
Why universality is needed: write $Y$ as a quotient of $X$ by the double arrow, add a morphism $Y'\to Y$.
\begin{CD} X' @>>> Y'\\ @VVV @VVV\\ X @>>> Y \end{CD}
Section of $X'\to Y'$ after base change; complete by fibre products; chase.
Need: $F(X)\to F(X')$ injective, i.e. the base-changed $X'\to X$ is at least an epimorphism (not nec. strict).
Canonical topology: universally strict epimorphic — more than needed here.
Same pattern for descent
$X\to Y$ of 2-descent if there is $Y'\to Y$ of effective descent dominated by it, with the right descent properties on the other arrows.
\text{2-descent}\;\Leftarrow\;(\text{2-descent},\ \text{1-descent},\ \text{0-descent})\text{ on the three arrows}
Universality is a very important condition.
(a) and (b) are equivalent whatever; (b)$\iff$(b$'$) was what I meant, misstated as (b$'$)$\Rightarrow$(c).
Nothing essential falls: strictly generating families meant (b) and (c$'$).
Correct statement of the theorem

Not: the full subcategory generated by $B(I)$ — too strong a condition; finite products of the $B(i)$.

Topos $\Rightarrow$ algebraic

T_C(E)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{lex}}(C,E)\quad\text{algebraic, finite inverse limits}
\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(\widehat C,E)\;\simeq\;\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{lex}}(C,E)
So $T_C$ is represented by $\widehat C$.
$R=\widetilde C$: morphisms $\widetilde C\to E$ = functors $C\to E$ left exact and continuous.
$T_R\subset T_C$ full sub-theory: left exact functors that send covering families to covering families.
